Article Title: 'Killed Nijjar for drug trafficking': Goldy Brar in leaked audio
Article Text:
Leaked audio captures Goldy Brar claiming Nijjar was targeted over alleged drug trafficking and its impact on young people

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a leaked audio conversation with pro-Khalistan terrorist Paramjit Singh Pamma, US-based gangster Goldy Brar has admitted to orchestrating the murder of Hardeep Singh Nijjar, a pro-Khalistan terrorist, in Canada in June 2023.Brar said Nijjar, whose killing had triggered a diplomatic crisis between India and Canada, was targeted over his "involvement in drug trafficking and promoting drug abuse". Intelligence sources confirmed the voice in the audio was Brar's.Brar, wanted in India for several killings - including that of singer Sidhu Moosewala - is heard saying Nijjar's promotion of drugs among teens irked him.This admission surfaced alongside the execution of Operation Hardball, a joint US-Canada law enforcement crackdown targeting transnational crime syndicates. The investigation had indicted Brar and Lawrence Bishnoi for orchestrating the killing of ‘HSN’ (short for Nijjar), reframing the high-profile assassination as a gangland hit rather than a state-sponsored killing.“Those who groomed and incited 16-to-17-year-olds to sell drugs... those who blackmailed young people into selling drugs and becoming informants... Nijjar supported and strengthened these individuals so that he could use them when necessary,” Brar is heard telling Pamma.“That’s why me and my team had to kill Nijjar, because these people were using young people to sell drugs. Good or bad, everyone has to face the consequences of their actions,” he added.Brar’s admission, which comes after his and Lawrence’s Op Hardball indictment in Nijjar’s murder, also reflected in Canadian police’s initial probe which hinted at gang rivalry. The probe also noted that a hit on Nijjar had been circulating for several weeks on an encrypted online site used to hire hitmen.Nijjar (45) was shot on June 18, 2023, in the parking lot of Guru Nanak Sikh Gurdwara, in Newton, Surrey. Six men and two vehicles were used in the attack. A CCTV video showed Nijjar’s grey pickup truck and a white sedan driving parallel in the parking lot of the gurdwara, seconds before the shooting started.Nijjar, the head of Khalistan Tiger Force (KTF), was replaced by his confidant Arshdeep Singh alias Arsh Dala. Interestingly, in the latest audio, Brar is also heard claiming the killing of Dala’s close associate, Sukhdool Singh alias Sukha Duneke, who was murdered in Winnipeg area in Sept 2023.
Article Summary: Leaked audio captures goldy brar claiming nijjar was targeted over alleged drug trafficking and its impact on young people. Intelligence sources confirmed the voice in the audio was brar's. Brar is wanted in india for several killings - including that of singer sidhu moosewala.

Article Title: Watch: Indian seafarers take cover as vessel passing through Hormuz came under attack in April
Article Text:
Seafarers take cover as small boats surround vessel in Hormuz

The Federation of Seafarers and Indian Seafarers Union (FSUI) has released an old video showing a vessel carrying 22 crew members, including 21 Indians, coming under attack in the Strait of Hormuz on April 22.The footage shows several small boats surrounding the vessel, an RPG being fired and seafarers rushing to the ship’s alleyways to take cover as the confrontation unfolded.The union also released images showing crew members taking cover while the vessel was under attack.“These were not pirates. They were naval forces of the IRGC,” the FSUI said in a post on X.The union added that the footage highlighted the risks faced by seafarers in the Strait of Hormuz, arguing that advisories and guidelines alone could not ensure their safety.“Innocent seafarers need the assured presence of naval forces to truly protect them,” the FSUI said.The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) recently said 166 Indian seafarers remained in the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz region, including 125 aboard six Indian-flagged vessels and 41 working on foreign-flagged ships.In an update on August 4, the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways said 3,972 Indian seafarers had been repatriated from the Gulf region, highlighting the scale of the effort to bring them out of the conflict zone.India is the world’s second-largest supplier of seafarers after the Philippines, with 311,936 personnel accounting for 12.16 per cent of the global maritime workforce, according to the BIMCO-ICS Seafarer Workforce Report 2026. Indian officers account for 13.41 per cent of the global officer workforce, while 171,218 Indian ratings make up 11.29 per cent of the global ratings workforce.The large presence of Indian seafarers in the region has also resulted in casualties since the Iran war began. Last month, the MEA said Indian seafarers had recorded the highest number of fatalities among all nationalities in attacks on commercial shipping.The government later informed Parliament that 10 Indian seafarers were among the 16 Indian nationals killed in the Middle East conflict.
Article Summary: Seafarers take cover as small boats surround vessel in hormuz. Video shows crew members taking cover while the vessel was under attack. “these were not pirates. They were naval forces of the irgc,” the fsui said.

Article Title: 'We fought wars with Pakistan too, but China will be India's main competitor': Ex-Army chief
Article Text:
General MM Naravane (Retd) on China and Pakistan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Former Army chief General MM Naravane (Retired) on Thursday described China as India's "main competitor" in the years ahead, despite India having fought wars with both China and Pakistan."Pakistan and China are a totally different ballgame. We have fought wars with both of them. We have unsettled borders. So they will always remain on our radar as a threat, as a challenge," PTI quoted Naravane as saying at a book launch event in New Delhi.However, he distinguished between the two, saying India's immediate focus on Pakistan was driven largely by the continuing threat of terrorism, while describing China as a "competitor" rather than an "enemy." He emphasised that he had "purposely" used the term "competitor" for China."We have fought major wars with Pakistan, and because of their continued support to terrorism, our attention is towards our western borders. But I think we are very clear that in the long term and in the years to come, China is going to be our main competitor. And I purposely use the word competitor and not enemy," Naravane said.Naravane, who was Chief of Army Staff during the 2020 Ladakh clashes with China and led India's response, further stated that the two countries would be competitors across multiple domains, including politics, economics, trade and military affairs."They are going to be our main competitor in all fields. Political, economic, trade, and of course military also. And wherever there is competition, there is always a little bit of conflict," the retired Army general observed.He emphasised that India should seek to manage such differences through dialogue and diplomatic mechanisms rather than resorting to force."It is up to us to try to resolve those conflicts, those differences, through the mechanisms of talks, dialogues. And taking recourse to the use of force should always be the last priority," he said.However, he also stressed that India must maintain credible military preparedness to deter any potential misadventure."There comes a moment when you realise that this is not going to happen. And therefore, you have to have a strong deterrence. That is why the armed forces have to be ready at all times. You have to have a strong deterrence to stop anybody from taking recourse to the use of force or any misadventure," he remarked.
Article Summary: General mm naravane (retd) on china and pakistan: "pakistan and china are a totally different ballgame" he emphasised that he had "purposely" used the term "competitor" for china.naravane was chief of army staff during the 2020 ladakh clashes with china.

Article Title: ‘Vishwasghaat’: CJP to review Centre’s promises, hints at fresh nationwide protest
Article Text:
CJP said the govt was yet to communicate steps being taken to fulfil assurances made during talks with the protesters.

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) will convene a meeting of its national working committee on Monday to review the Centre’s commitments that led to the withdrawal of its nationwide agitation on July 25, with the outfit saying that any attempt to backtrack could amount to “vishwasghaat” (betrayal) with the country’s youth.The CJP said the government was yet to formally communicate the steps being taken to fulfil assurances made during talks with the protesters. It said the committee would consider all options to secure implementation of the commitments, including the possibility of launching another peaceful nationwide agitation.“The CJP called off its agitation in good faith because the government gave its word to the young people of this country,” CJP said, adding that it would not allow that “good faith” to be mistaken for “weakness”.The CJP has also asked students, young citizens, supporters and volunteers to remain prepared for the outcome of Monday’s meeting.The warning comes days after the Supreme Court, on August 18, sought a consolidated list of FIRs registered against students and protesters across the country. According to the CJP, the court asked the Centre three times to provide the list so it could consider exercising its powers under Article 142 to quash the cases.“Despite the court repeatedly asking for this list, the Union government did not commit to providing it,” the CJP said.The party said that any attempt to “dilute, delay, reinterpret or dishonour” the commitments, would be seen as “vishwasghaat” (betrayal) with the country's youthThe outfit said its co-convener Saurav Das and legal affairs lead Ratna Singh raised concerns after the hearing that the government appeared to be “cheating” the younger generation by failing to act on the commitments made when the agitation was withdrawn.Those assurances included withdrawal or quashing of FIRs linked to the protests, a guarantee that students and peaceful protesters would not face punitive action in future, and compensation for families of NEET-UG candidates who died by suicide after the examination was cancelled in May following paper-leak allegations.Meanwhile, fresh guidelines issued to Delhi Police personnel have advised officers to remain calm during protests, avoid provocation and assume that their conduct will be recorded and scrutinised.The directions follow allegations of police excesses during the CJP’s Jantar Mantar protest last month. “Your anger is their satisfaction and content for them to portray you as villains," the guidelines say.The advisory asks personnel to avoid arguments with protesters and not react to taunts, songs, placards or attempts to provoke them. It also stresses assisting protesters who fall ill or are injured and ensuring unobstructed movement for ambulances, schoolchildren and elderly people.(With inputs from PTI)
Article Summary: Cjp said the govt was yet to communicate steps being taken to fulfil assurances made during talks with the protesters. It said the committee would consider all options to secure implementation of the commitments, including the possibility of launching another peaceful nationwide agitation.

Article Title: Ex-IAF vice-chief Kapoor says India’s 4.5-gen Tejas may not have relevance in 2030s, country must partner with global consortiums like FCAS or GCAP for 6th-gen programme
Article Text:
Air Marshal Kapoor (Retd) did not totally rule out the role of Tejas Mk2 in future

NEW DELHI: Less than two months after retirement as the IAF's vice chief, Air Marshal Nagesh Kapoor (Retd) has slammed the delay in the delivery of Tejas (LCA) fighter jet by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited to the air force, saying, “why must it be that a machine that was promised to us so many years back with a certain set of capabilities continues to be denied to us on one pretext or the other”.In an interview to NDTV, the IAF veteran said, “Why must we be hamstrung because someone somewhere has not been able to keep their promises?”The delivery of the indigenous LCA Tejas Mk1A jets by HAL to the IAF has faced multi-year delays, primarily caused by late supplies of F404-IN20 engines by American GE company, complex mission software validation, and stringent operational requirements set by the IAF.When asked if advanced Tejas Mk-2 may be operationally relevant when it starts entering service in big numbers in mid 2030s at a time when China is already raising its fleet of its 5th-generation fighter jet, the former vice-chief said, “No, operationally, definitely no.”With China on its way to deploying 500 5th-generation J-20 fighters by 2030, India is still struggling to get the delivery of the first squadron by 4.5-generation Tejas Mk1A. Though the IAF had placed orders for a total of 180 Tejas Mk1A fighter jets long ago, HAL hopes to deliver the first 18-25 Tejas Mk1A only by March 2027.Air Marshal Kapoor (Retd) did not totally rule out the role of Tejas Mk2 in future when he said, “You can have a certain number of those 5th generation and 6th generation fighters, but given the size of the country, you won't be able to deploy them everywhere.So those gaps which continue to remain to be filled will have to be filled by this class of aircraft.” “I want Tejas Mk-2 to come, I want India’s 5th-gen AMCA to come. But they must come at a much faster speed,” he said.When asked about Russia’s 5th-gen fighter jet Su-57, the former vice-chief said when the Russian fighter is compared to western jets like American F-35, western jets have an edge over the Su-57 as they have better avionics and stealth.Air Marshal Kapoor (Retd) suggested that India should partner with an European consortium working on state-of-the-art sixth generation platforms. “There are other things that are happening — why not join FCAS (Future Combat Air System is the European programme for 6th generation jet under development by French Dassault Aviation, Airbus and Indra Sistemas) Why not GCAP (Global Combat Air Programme is a multinational initiative led by Italy, Japan, and UK to jointly develop a sixth-generation jet).“'You are probably going with a consortium which has got a good record of delivery, of development. Why go through this Gen 4, Gen 4.5 steps when you know the next best thing is already being thought of and why not just join up there?,” the IAF veteran said.His comments underline the difficult choices facing India’s air power planners: meeting immediate squadron requirements while ensuring that indigenous programmes do not fall behind the rapid evolution of military aviation technology.
Article Summary: Air marshal kapoor (retd) did not totally rule out the role of tejas mk2 in future. He suggested that india should partner with an european consortium working on state-of-the-art sixth generation platforms. His comments underline the difficult choices facing india’s air power planners.

Article Title: How Ananta Maharaj row exposed old fault lines over Netaji
Article Text:
Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose

The 'war criminal' letter

Conundrum

What Nehru said on Netaji

Congress: from president to rebel

An Indian Pilgrim

The Indian Struggle

From comrades to 'Fifth Column'

How INA played a key role

Renkoji temple

From debating Bose to claiming Bose

PM Modi unveiling Netaji statue

For the longest time, January 23 in 1990s Kolkata would mean small street-side political meetings where leaders of all hues would ask the youth to draw inspiration from Netaji's patriotism and ideals on his birthday. Netaji was one of the most prominent politicians who disappeared before India became independent, and yet left a firm imprint on people's minds. The conversation around him was often about what people knew and what, they believed, had been concealed, be it the mystery surrounding his disappearance, the classified files or his political views, which parties have tried to appropriate and yet conveniently stayed away from at different times. His own political party, the Forward Bloc, a junior partner in the long-running Left Front government in West Bengal, is now a pale shadow of its glory days. Yet Netaji remains an iconic hero not only in Bengal but across India. BJP Rajya Sabha MP Nagendra Ray, better known as Ananta Maharaj, has apologised for his vitriolic remarks on Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose. The dust will settle soon, but what is unlikely to be ironed out any time soon is the uneasy relationship political parties in Bengal have had with the state's most enduring nationalist icon.Ananta Maharaj rattled the hornet's nest by questioning Bose's contribution to the freedom struggle and the Indian National Army, was reported to have called him a "war criminal", and claimed the INA consisted essentially of British-Indian soldiers "captured and handed over by Germany". He also asked what the INA had achieved for Indian independence. This prompted swift action, with the Suvendu Adhikari government withdrawing the Banga Bibhushan , Bengal's highest civilian honour, which Mamata Banerjee's government had conferred on him. Subsequently, Ananta apologised.As a parting shot, the Rajya Sabha MP insisted his claims rested on material in the National Archives and invoked Jawaharlal Nehru over the "war criminal" description. This calls for a dispassionate look at what history actually says about these claims.Material declassified in 2016 revived a long-circulating claim that Nehru had called Bose Britain's "war criminal". The files contained a later account of an alleged Nehru dictation, not an authenticated original Nehru-to-Attlee letter.The archival trail leads to testimony by Shyam Lal Jain, Nehru's former stenographer, who claimed decades afterwards that Nehru had dictated a December 1945 communication to British Prime Minister Clement Attlee referring to "Subhas Chandra Bose, your war criminal".Nehru's own recorded words point in the opposite direction. On August 29, 1945, when an American journalist put it to him that Bose should be treated as a war criminal, Nehru replied: "I resent the suggestion that Subhas Bose should be dealt with as a war criminal." In April 1956, Nehru would again write internally that "the question of War Criminals does not arise" while discussing the Netaji inquiry.There is, however, an intriguing archival footnote. In, Chandrachur Ghose and Anuj Dhar cite a 1956 Ministry of External Affairs file created after notices of parliamentary questions asking whether Bose was still regarded as a war criminal. The questions followed Forward Bloc leader Muthuramalingam Thevar's demand before the Netaji Inquiry Committee that the government clarify whether Bose's name figured on such a list.The first response recorded in the file came from historian Sarvepalli Gopal, then head of the MEA's Historical Division. After consulting the Law and Defence ministries, Gopal wrote: "All records related to Subhas Bose were destroyed in 1947, but as far as we know Bose was not publicly designated a war criminal." The Khosla inquiry would later record an even more categorical government position: inquiries with Indian missions indicated that Bose's name had never figured on a war-criminal list.Ghose, speaking to TOI, is equally categorical that he has found no archival evidence establishing that Bose was a war criminal. He points out, however, that such an allegation was indeed made on oath by a pendant before the Khosla Commission.One thing, though, Ananta Maharaj does get right, Bose did not create the first INA. The INA initially took shape in Japanese-controlled Southeast Asia in 1942 under Captain Mohan Singh, built around British Indian Army soldiers who had fallen into Japanese hands during the Malaya campaign and the fall of Singapore. It broke down amid disputes over Japanese control. Rash Behari Bose began reorganising the movement in early 1943. Subhas Bose arrived in Southeast Asia that July and took over, after which the INA expanded dramatically in scale and political clout. So while Netaji wasn't the founder, he became the beating heart of the INA.The BJP MP appears to have conflated two different episodes from Netaji's life in making his claim about Germany. Before reaching Southeast Asia, Bose had run a separate military project in Germany, the Indian Legion, drawing substantially on Indian prisoners of war captured by Axis forces in North Africa.Bose's quarrel with Congress had multiple layers, some driven by the power politics of the time and others by the ideological strands to which its top leaders belonged. Bose rose to the top of the party, becoming Congress president at Haripura in 1938 and standing for a second term the following year, when he defeated Pattabhi Sitaramayya, the candidate identified with Gandhi's camp, by 203 votes. Gandhi's response became the stuff of legend: Sitaramayya's defeat, he said, was "more mine than his".That was merely the start of the churn. Twelve of the 15 members of the Congress Working Committee resigned, the Tripuri session deepened the crisis, and Bose eventually stepped down. Nehru and Gandhi disagreed with his more confrontational line against Britain, yet Nehru was unhappy at the prospect of Bose simply being pushed out. In April 1939, he wrote to Gandhi that doing so would be "an exceedingly wrong step".The war drove the two much further apart. Bose read Britain's vulnerability as India's opportunity, a calculation that took him to Nazi Germany and then to Japanese-controlled Southeast Asia. Nehru fiercely opposed that route. His respect for Bose's patriotism, however, remained intact. Speaking on Bose's birthday in January 1946, he said: "I never for a moment doubted that he was a brave soldier in the struggle for freedom. " He praised the communal unity of the INA and called the force a "legend".Chandra Kumar Bose, Netaji's grand-nephew, makes another distinction. Recalling what his father Amiya Nath Bose, Sarat Bose's son and therefore Netaji's nephew told him, Chandra says Bose's dealings with Hitler and Tojo should not be confused with ideological admiration for either. According to him, Netaji did not like either leader; the alliances were instruments towards what he saw as the overriding objective of Indian independence. Chandra argues that Bose's ownandremain essential reading for anyone trying to understand his political philosophy.The INA lost the war but gained widespread acceptance afterwards. The Red Fort trials of Shah Nawaz Khan, Prem Kumar Sahgal and Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon in late 1945 produced an outpouring of public sympathy. Nehru joined their defence and donned the barrister's robes after decades away from legal practice.Chandra also points to a famous anecdote about former British PM Clement Attlee. In a letter written two decades after their meeting, P B Chakravartti, former acting governor of West Bengal, recalled Attlee telling him during a 1956 visit that the INA's impact on the loyalty of the armed forces, followed by the Royal Indian Navy revolt, had been important in Britain's decision to leave. When asked about Gandhi's influence on the final decision, Chakravartti recalled Attlee describing it as "minimal".Before the war, Bose occupied ground that overlapped with the Indian Left. He belonged to the radical wing of nationalism and worked at building alliances with communists and other Left formations in Bengal.The war ended that. Hitler's attack on the Soviet Union in June 1941 fundamentally changed the Communist reading of the conflict and, by the turn of 1941-42, the Communist Party had moved towards its "People's War" line. Bose was moving in the opposite direction, towards Axis help against Britain.P C Joshi's 1945 defence of the Communist position named the Forward Bloc, along with the Congress Socialist Party and Trotskyists, as groups that "made the Fifth Column, the agents of the Jap invader".The original wartime publication carrying the exact words "Tojo's dog" is harder to pin down. But when CPI general secretary A B Bardhan apologised in 2010 for the party's historical assessment of Bose, contemporary reports recalled that the undivided CPI had denounced him as an "imperialist agent" and "Tojo's dog".The rethink had started much earlier. Chandra Bose recalls Jyoti Basu publicly acknowledging the Communist misreading of Netaji. Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee followed in 2003, calling it a "great mistake" and saying,"I am apologising for our mistaken assessment of Netaji," while continuing to disagree with Bose's Axis strategy.The Ananta row was not the first this year to reopen Netaji-era wounds. In July, Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya called Forward Bloc members "goons" and alleged that they had pelted stones at Syama Prasad Mookerjee while he was addressing a gathering at Mohammed Ali Park during the 1940 Calcutta Corporation election. He also subsequently claimed that Mookerjee had appealed to Subhas and Sarat Bose over the condition of Hindus in eastern Bengal and received no response.Forward Bloc called Samik's account a distortion Ghose says the real history was more complicated. Before the 1940 Corporation election, there were negotiations for an understanding between Bose's camp and the Hindu Mahasabha. They failed. Bose's group subsequently entered into a municipal pact with the Muslim League in April 1940, a tactical arrangement that immediately became ammunition for his opponents.Bose and Mookerjee were certainly adversaries. Mookerjee's diary records Bose warning him that if he tried to build the Hindu Mahasabha as a rival organisation in Bengal, Bose would see it broken, "by force if need be". Yet Chandrachur Ghose and Chandra Bose agree on another aspect that is often lost in today's retelling that the two remained remarkably civil towards each other despite the ideological battle.Mookerjee had long-standing links with the Bose family, intervened with authorities over the treatment of Subhas and Sarat while they were detained, and his writings spoke of "admiration and affection" for Subhas alongside political disagreement.Chandra adds a family footnote. After Bose's expulsion from Presidency College, Sir Asutosh Mookerjee, Syama Prasad's father, played a role in enabling him to resume his studies. Bose ultimately entered Scottish Church College.Chandra also points to Syama Prasad's participation in Fazlul Huq's Bengal ministry. In other words, Bengal's politics in those years was full of tactical arrangements that don't align well with clean ideological lines drawn retrospectively.Ghose goes a step further, arguing that newspapers aligned with the pro-Gandhi camp, already hostile to Bose for creating a new political organisation, also helped amplify the Bose-Mookerjee rift.There is another Netaji dispute on which governments and even members of his own family have not always spoken in one voice, regarding the urn at Tokyo's Renkoji Temple, which is said to contain remains carried from Taipei following the reported plane crash of August 18, 1945.The majority report of the Shah Nawaz Committee and the later Khosla Commission supported the plane-crash account. Prime Minister Morarji Desai told Parliament in 1978 that contradictions and later material meant their conclusions could not be treated as decisive. The Justice M K Mukherjee Commission subsequently concluded that Bose was dead but had not died in the alleged plane crash and that the Renkoji remains were not his.Chandra Bose's own position has changed dramatically. He once questioned the crash theory, but after the declassification exercise came to the opposite conclusion. In 2024, he publicly said that the evidence from 10 national and international inquiries, taken together with the released files, convinced him that Netaji died in the August 18, 1945 crash. He now says Japan deserves credit for preserving the remains with dignity for eight decades, but that the time has come to bring them home.Ghose, in his conversation with TOI, called for an anthropological examination of the Renkoji material, saying conventional DNA recovery may no longer be viable and insisting that any examination should be conducted under neutral observation.In 2015, Mamata Banerjee's government released 64 Netaji files running to 12,744 pages and challenged the Centre to open its own records. The Modi government followed with a phased central release, beginning with 100 digitised files on January 23, 2016.Then came the wrangling over what to call his birth anniversary. The Left had Desh Prem Divas. Mamata chose Desh Nayak Diwas. The Centre declared January 23 Parakram Diwas in 2021. In 2022, Modi unveiled Bose's statue near India Gate and said Netaji had been forgotten after Independence, his ideas and even the symbols associated with him ignored.Chandra Bose says this is precisely the problem with the politics around historical icons that their names are invoked while their ideology is often ignored. He is dismissive of Samik Bhattacharya's recent comments about Forward Bloc. Why, he asks, must one leader be pulled down simply to prop up another?Parties of all hues have tried to appropriate different facets of Netaji's life. The BJP has highlighted his military courage and uncompromising nationalism. The Left can point to his socialism, and anti-imperialism. Congress has the bragging rights of Netaji having been its two-time president. Ghose puts the problem another way. Bose was, as the title of his biography has it, an "inconvenient nationalist". Allegiance to the nation, he says, was the one overriding constant in Bose's politics.That is what makes the Ananta Maharaj row worth more than a news cycle. While he lived, Bose was too difficult for any political establishment to hold comfortably. Since his disappearance, his legacy has been too valuable for any of them to concede.
Article Summary: Netaji subhas chandra bose was one of the most prominent politicians who disappeared before india became independent. The conversation around him was often about what people knew and what, they believed, had been concealed.

Article Title: No more boarding pass stamps: New immigration rule for international flyers from Sept 1
Article Text:
International travelers will soon need e-boarding passes on smartphones for immigration clearance. Physical boarding passes will no longer be stamped by immigration authorities from September one. This change aims to streamline the process and reduce passenger inconvenience. A pilot project is also underway to eliminate immigration stamping for Indian passport holders. The Bureau of Immigration is implementing these modernization efforts across airports.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Passengers travelling abroad will reportedly need an e-boarding pass on their smartphones for immigration clearance from September one, as immigration authorities plan to replace the physical boarding pass, officials said.The decision was taken after the Bureau of Immigration (BOI) under the ministry of home affairs (MHA) found that the physical stamping of boarding passes, required for immigration, was inconvenient for passengers."The matter has been examined by the BOI and it has now been decided to do away with the mandatory requirement of physical boarding passes and the stamping of boarding passes at immigration counters at all international airports in the country", according to officials who spoke to PTI.“Improper or incorrect” stamping also led to errors in reading boarding passes, prompting the decision to do away with this procedure, they added.However, while physical boarding passes will continue to be accepted, they will not be stamped by the immigration authorities from September 1.Security officials said international travellers were also no longer having their boarding passes stamped by the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) during individual frisking. The passes were instead required to be produced only for clearance by immigration authorities.Notably, CISF had stopped stamping boarding passes for both domestic and international passengers several years ago.According to the officials, a pilot project is also underway to eliminate the stamping of immigration entry and exit for Indian passport holders. The process is expected to be implemented across Indian airports soon after the pilot exercise is complete.
Article Summary: International travelers will soon need e-boarding passes on smartphones for immigration clearance. Physical boarding passes will no longer be stamped by immigration authorities from september one. This change aims to streamline the process and reduce passenger inconvenience.

Article Title: Panama-flagged ship sinks off Odisha, 2 rescued; search on for 22: Shipping minister
Article Text:
2 survivors from Panama-flagged vessel rescued, search ops underway: Sonowal

Two survivors have been rescued from a Panama-flagged cargo vessel that sank in the Bay of Bengal with 24 people on board, while search-and-rescue operations remain underway for the other crew members, shipping and waterways minister Sarbananda Sonowal said on Sunday.The vessel, MV Ocean Winner, was carrying 72,100 metric tonnes of iron ore from Odisha's Paradip Port and sank about 230-240 nautical miles from the coast, according to officials and reports cited by PTI earlier. The vessel had a length overall of 225 metres and a width of 32.26 metres.“Deeply concerned by the unfortunate incident involving MV OCEAN WINNER off the coast of Odisha. The Panama-flagged vessel was carrying iron ore from Paradip Port to China,” Sonowal said in a post on X.“All agencies are coordinating closely and search and rescue efforts are underway,” he said.Sonowal added, “2 survivors have been successfully rescued and are being given medical care; their rank and identity are currently being verified.”The Indian Coast Guard (ICG) intensified its search after losing communication with the vessel on Saturday. The ship had 24 crew members, 20 Chinese nationals, three Myanmar nationals and one Bangladeshi national.The Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre (MRCC) diverted MT Aisopos, a commercial vessel in the vicinity, to assist in the search. The vessel recovered two survivors from two life rafts at about 8 pm, officials said.The ICG had also deployed two vessels from Sri Vijaya Puram, formerly known as Port Blair, for the search-and-rescue operation, Coast Guard spokesperson Commandant Amit Uniyal said.The vessel had left the Paradip coast at 10.42 pm on August 20, carrying iron ore fines, according to officials. An initial report by India's maritime authorities said it was bound for China, while other government information indicated Singapore as its destination.The cause of the sinking was not immediately known.Search operations are continuing to locate the remaining crew members, with maritime agencies coordinating efforts in the area.

National Security Advisor Ajit Doval is set to arrive in Beijing on Monday for the 25th round of India-China Special Representatives talks on the boundary issue with his Chinese counterpart Wang Yi.The talks are scheduled to take place on Tuesday, according to official sources, as cited by PTI.The talks come ahead of the expected visit of Chinese President Xi Jinping to India for the BRICS summit in New Delhi on September 12-13.While Beijing has not officially confirmed Xi’s participation, officials on both sides remain optimistic that he will attend, potentially opening the way for a meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi to discuss steps to advance bilateral ties.Doval and Wang serve as the designated Special Representatives for the boundary talks mechanism, established in 2003 to seek a comprehensive resolution to the India-China border dispute, which stretches 3,488 km.Although the mechanism has not resolved the boundary dispute, officials on both sides consider it a useful platform for managing recurring tensions and addressing differences between the two countries.Doval and Wang last met in August 2025 on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Tianjin.Ahead of the upcoming talks in Beijing, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar on Saturday reiterated that peace and tranquillity along the border are essential for maintaining good relations between India and China.External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said earlier this month that India views issues concerning the border areas with China as “most serious” and stressed that maintaining peace and tranquillity along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) is of “utmost importance”. He said the situation along the frontier would determine the overall trajectory of India-China relations.New Delhi had earlier rejected Beijing’s criticism of India’s decision to assign official names to 27 places and geographical features in Arunachal Pradesh, asserting that the state is an “inalienable and integral” part of India and that nothing can change this “indisputable reality”.China, which claims Arunachal Pradesh as part of South Tibet, has issued its own set of names for places in the region since 2017.India has dismissed the practice as “vain and preposterous”, maintaining that such actions cannot alter the “undeniable” reality that Arunachal Pradesh “was, is, and will” always remain an integral part of India.

NEW DELHI: Chief Justice Surya Kant on Saturday proposed ‘Nyaya Setu’ for the BRICS+ bloc for seamless exchange of judgments of the highest courts of the bloc countries and allowing young judges to share dais with judges of partner country jurisdictions to learn the best practices.Speaking the BRICS+ Legal forum organised by Bar Association of India, CJI Kant placed a twin proposal: first, a BRICS+ judicial fellowship, allowing early career judges to sit, even briefly, in one another’s courts; and second, a shared jurisprudence repository, drawing on India's own considerable investment in digitised case law, so that a judgment written in New Delhi or Brasilia or Pretoria need not wait years to inform a bench elsewhere facing an identical question.“Let it be ‘Nyaya Setu’, a ‘Bridge Of Justice’ that connects eleven legal traditions which have mutually agreed that trust should be cultivated deliberately rather than awaited passively. Let us, therefore, commit to a future where institutions are not fortresses of formality but bridges of trust, where our united efforts illuminate a path of mutual harmony and prosperity,” he said.Explaining the importance of rule of law in building a vibrant economy, CJI Kant said the marriage between the rule of law and favourable economic conditions engenders ‘Nyaya-nomics’, or economics of justice.“It is a fact that consistent adjudication and trust in the process reduce the cost of each transaction built upon it, thereby levelling the playing field for market forces, and in turn, making way for growth,” he said.He said when SC upheld the validity of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), and later affirmed that the commercial wisdom of a Committee o Creditors deserved primacy over years of open-ended litigation, it was emphasising that “capital recycled quickly is capital that returns, and capital trapped in litigation for a decade rarely does.”The CJI said India rose from among the bottom quarter of the World Bank’s ease of doing business rankings into its top hundred, and enforcing a contract in this country stopped being a byword for delay. “To my mind, a courtroom that keeps its word quickly becomes a country the world is willing to trust with its capital,” he said.
Article Summary: Chief justice surya kant proposes ‘nyaya setu’ for the brics+ bloc. It would allow seamless exchange of judgments of the highest courts of the bloc countries. Young judges would be able to share dais with judges of partner country jurisdictions.

Former India captains Sunil Gavaskar , Kapil Dev and Dilip Vengsarkar are among 21 former international cricket captains who have written to Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, asking for proper medical treatment and welfare of jailed former Pakistan Prime Minister and World Cup-winning captain Imran Khan.The letter was initiated by former Australia captain Greg Chappell. It is the second appeal by former international captains seeking humane treatment and medical care for the 73-year-old Khan.The captains said they were "not seek to adjudicate Pakistan’s domestic legal processes but believed that ensuring a court-ordered medical process was completed was a basic matter of decency".The former captains made three specific requests to the Pakistan government:They asked that the medical board ordered by Pakistan's Supreme Court, including Imran Khan's personal doctors, be allowed to complete a full and independent assessment of his health, especially the reported loss of vision in his right eye.The captains urged the government to honour the Supreme Court's order allowing Khan's family to meet him every week without interruption or administrative delays.They requested that any medical treatment recommended after the assessment be provided without delay.Khan has been in jail since 2023. Late last year, he and his wife were sentenced to 17 years in prison on corruption charges, which they both deny.On Friday, Khan was taken back to jail just hours after being moved to Islamabad's private Shifa International Hospital for medical checks ordered by the Supreme Court.
